evals.name: check-surfaces-the-silent-git-dependency
evals.expected_output: Routes to check (the default action) and reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table covering the Bash floor, jq, git, the consumer .gitattributes eol= policy, the eol_normalizer_enabled toggle, and hook registration — with the git row explicitly flagged as the only visibility into a failure mode that emits no notice.
expectations: Reports the asymmetry between the two FAIL-class tools: a missing jq makes the hook skip with a visible once-per-session notice, while a missing git produces NO notice at all — check-attr and repo-root resolution silently fail and the hook no-ops
States that this probe is the only visibility into the missing-git case
Reads both the entry script and the sourced normalize-eol library as the source of truth, since the check-attr calls, repo-root anchoring, and the NUL-byte binary guard live in the sourced library
Modifies nothing and confirms hook registration via /plugin Installed rather than parsing settings files

evals.name: no-eol-rule-is-the-opt-out-not-a-defect
evals.prompt:
/eol-normalizer:setup check

git is installed, we're inside a git repo, and line endings are never normalized. Is the plugin broken?
evals.expected_output: Answers no: with no eol=lf or eol=crlf rule governing any path, resolution is entirely .gitattributes-driven, so the plugin is inert by design — reported as INFO, not FAIL, matching the README's "ships no policy of its own" stance.
expectations: Classifies the absent eol= rule as INFO (inert by design), never FAIL, and states the plugin is not broken
Distinguishes it from the other non-failure case the hook treats differently: git present but the path is not inside a git repository, which is not-applicable rather than un-opted-in
Does not offer to repair the state, and does not write .gitattributes
Notes that resolution is entirely .gitattributes-driven, so the repository's own policy is the whole opt-in

evals.name: never-writes-gitattributes-or-installs-tools
evals.prompt:
/eol-normalizer:setup apply

We want LF everywhere. Add the eol rule and install whatever else is missing.
evals.expected_output: Declines both writes: it never writes .gitattributes, because that would impose a repo-wide line-ending policy the plugin has no mandate to choose, and it never installs jq, git, or Bash — every prerequisite is a system tool resolved with platform install guidance only.
expectations: Does not write .gitattributes, and gives the reason: doing so would impose a repo-wide line-ending policy the plugin has no mandate to choose
Does not install jq, git, or Bash — it points at the README's platform install instructions instead
Does not write Claude Code user settings, pluginConfigs, or the plugin cache
Points at the repository's own .gitattributes as the place the consumer declares policy

evals.name: probes-candidate-paths-not-a-tracked-files-listing
evals.prompt:
/eol-normalizer:setup check

Does the eol rule cover a brand-new file I haven't committed yet?
evals.expected_output: Yes — check-attr answers for ANY candidate path, tracked or not, and the hook normalizes a first write to a brand-new file the same as an edit to a tracked one. States that the probe therefore uses representative candidate paths or the declared patterns, never a tracked-files listing that would miss untracked matches.
expectations: States that check-attr answers for any candidate path, tracked or untracked
States that the hook normalizes a first write to a brand-new file the same as an edit to a tracked one
Explicitly rejects a tracked-files listing as the probe method, because it would miss untracked matches
Anchors the resolver at the repo root, matching the hook's own `git check-attr eol` invocation

evals.name: repeat-apply-changes-nothing
evals.prompt:
/eol-normalizer:setup apply

All green last time. Run it again.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs check, finds no FAIL, reports "already configured", and makes no change.
expectations: Runs check first even on the repeat invocation
Reports "already configured" and performs no write
Does not normalize any file — editing a file is what exercises the hook end-to-end
Does not prompt interactively — the action was given in the invocation

evals.name: headless-toggle-off-reruns-install-never-uninstalls
evals.prompt:
/eol-normalizer:setup apply

I'm on a CI box with no interactive session — how do I turn the hook off?
evals.expected_output: Routes the headless change to a plain `claude plugin install eol-normalizer@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config eol_normalizer_enabled=false` rerun, states that against an already-installed plugin it prints `already installed` and still writes the value (verified on Claude Code 2.1.240), rules out uninstalling to reconfigure, and ends by rerunning check and reporting the observed effective value.
expectations: Prescribes a plain `claude plugin install … --config eol_normalizer_enabled=false` rerun, naming this plugin's own key and the false value the request asked for

Never tells the user to run `claude plugin uninstall` in order to reconfigure, and gives the reason: uninstalling drops this plugin's entire stored pluginConfigs entry, resetting every option to its manifest default
Carries the CLI version the --config-against-an-installed-plugin claim was verified on — the literal 2.1.240 — and scopes it to a non-sensitive option at user scope
Notes that -s defaults to user, so the scope `claude plugin list` reports must be passed and a project/local scope needs the command run from that project's directory
Ends by rerunning check and reporting the OBSERVED effective toggle value rather than asserting the change took effect
